test_title: PYST 23: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements best describes the Indian Union Cabinet’s role in legislation?

options.text: The Cabinet is the only law-making body in India.
The Cabinet gives final shape to government bills and prepares the legislative agenda.
The Cabinet enacts laws without any involvement of any house of the Indian Parliament.
The Cabinet has judicial authority over legislations surpassing the judiciary.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Cabinet gives final shape to government bills and prepares the legislative agenda.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Union Cabinet plays a key role in the legislative process by **formulating and finalizing government bills** before they are introduced in Parliament.
 
• It is responsible for **preparing the legislative agenda**, which outlines the government’s priority bills to be discussed in Parliament.
 
• The Cabinet ensures that proposed legislations align with **government policies and objectives**.
 
• After the Cabinet approves a bill, it is introduced in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha for deliberation and eventual enactment.
 
• The Cabinet does not have the authority to enact laws directly; it acts as an **executive body** within the structure of parliamentary democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Cabinet**:

 
 
• The Union Cabinet is a part of the Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister of India.
 
• It is responsible for the formulation of policies and implementation of laws in India.
 
• The Cabinet operates under the framework of the Indian Constitution, which establishes the principle of collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process in India**:
 
 
• Legislation in India involves drafting bills, deliberation in Parliament, and Presidential assent.
 
• The government primarily introduces bills that reflect its policies and priorities.
 
 
 
• **Role of Parliament**:
 
 
• Both the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) deliberate on bills to ensure comprehensive scrutiny.
 
• The Parliament enacts laws, while the Cabinet facilitates the process by preparing and proposing bills.
 
 
 
• **Checks and Balances**:
 
 
• The Cabinet cannot bypass the legislative authority of Parliament.
 
• This ensures a balance of power between the executive, legislative, and judicial branches of government.
